subject: Intermittent stream latency spikes impacting agent UI
messages:
From: Megan Todd <megan.todd@brightcart.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood-inference.com
Cc: BrightCart Ops <ops@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent stream latency spikes impacting agent UI

Hi Jonas,

We're seeing repeated latency spikes on Redwood's streaming endpoint that are disrupting our live agent UI. Between 09:05 and 09:10 PT this morning sessions in us-west-2 experienced multi-second gaps in token delivery (UI shows streaming freeze for 6-12s). This is affecting ~12% of active conversations and causing agents to reload.

We captured a few request ids: req_20260815_8a2f, req_20260815_8a31, req_20260815_8a3d. I'm attaching a short list of sample request ids and timestamps.

Can you confirm whether there's anything on your side (edge congestion, rollout, config change) and share immediate mitigations we can apply?

Thanks,
Megan
Megan Todd
VP, Product
BrightCart

From: jonas_weber@redwood-inference.com
To: Megan Todd <megan.todd@brightcart.com>, BrightCart Ops <ops@brightcart.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2026-08-15T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent stream latency spikes impacting agent UI

Thanks for the heads up, Megan — sorry for the disruption. We're investigating now. Initial notes: we don't have any scheduled rollouts affecting us-west-2 at that window but we'll triage infra telemetry immediately.

Short-term mitigations you can try (low-risk, on your side):
- Enable a 5000ms client-side streaming timeout + retry logic for streaming chunks (if a chunk stalls, retry once after 500ms).
- As a fallback, switch to the non-streaming generate endpoint for high-priority agent flows while we triage (slightly higher latency but avoids chunk stalls).
- If you can, set your client to accept smaller chunk sizes (max_chunk_bytes=4096) to reduce per-chunk retransmit weight.

Marissa (cc'd) — can you pull edge metrics for us-west-2 from 09:00–09:30 PT and check for queueing/backpressure or kernel restarts?

I'll keep you updated every 30 minutes until we have a root cause.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood-inference.com, Megan Todd <megan.todd@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent stream latency spikes impacting agent UI

Forwarding initial findings.

On 09:00–09:30 PT we see short-lived increases in per-token emit latency on edge shard us-west-2-e-17 (spike window aligns with your timestamps). Cause appears to be a transient backpressure event from a noisy tenant saturating our GPU I/O path on that shard, causing queue growth and delayed token emission for co-located streams. We did not observe kernel crashes but the KV cache eviction cadence increased and some stream sessions experienced delayed token emits of 6–12s.

Immediate remediation applied by infra at 09:22 PT: temporary routing isolation of the noisy tenant and increased fairness-weight for streaming RPCs on affected shard. That reduced error rates by ~80% within 6 minutes.

Recommended actions for BrightCart (config snippets attached):
1) Client-side: implement short streaming retransmit window + single retry on chunk gap (see attached temporary-fallback-config-snippet.txt).
2) Server-side: we recommend you enable graceful fallback in your routing policy so the client can automatically fall back to the non-streaming generate endpoint for sessions where chunking stalls >3s. This is a config toggle in our console under Conversation->Fallbacks.
3) If you use long-lived connections, set heartbeat pings every 15s to detect stalls earlier.

We'll provide a full incident timeline and postmortem once we've completed log correlation and root cause analysis.

Attachments: temporary-fallback-config-snippet.txt (text)

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Megan Todd <megan.todd@brightcart.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood-inference.com
Cc: BrightCart Ops <ops@brightcart.com>, marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2026-08-15T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent stream latency spikes impacting agent UI

Thanks — we applied the client-side retry and tightened max_chunk_bytes per Marissa's snippet. We're seeing a noticeable reduction in freezes (estimated affected sessions dropped from ~12% to ~2%), but a handful of enterprise flows still show intermittent pauses.

Two questions: 1) Do we qualify for a service credit under our SLA for the window where agent productivity was impacted? 2) When can we expect a permanent mitigation so we don't have to keep relying on the non-streaming fallback?

I'll hold off on switching everything to non-streaming for now but would like a timeline for when a fix is scheduled.

-Megan
From: jonas_weber@redwood-inference.com
To: Megan Todd <megan.todd@brightcart.com>, BrightCart Ops <ops@brightcart.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2026-08-16T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent stream latency spikes impacting agent UI — incident summary and next steps

Megan — thank you for the quick collaboration and for applying the workaround. Below is our interim post-incident summary and next steps. Full postmortem and remediation plan attached.

Summary (what happened)
- On 2026-08-15 09:05–09:30 PT, us-west-2 edge shard us-west-2-e-17 experienced transient backpressure due to a noisy tenant's large batched workloads saturating GPU I/O paths. This increased KV eviction rate and introduced token emit delays (6–12s) for co-located streaming sessions.

Actions taken
- 09:22 PT: infra applied routing isolation and fairness adjustments to the noisy tenant (temporary mitigation).
- 09:28 PT: SRE recommended client-side retransmit + fallback; BrightCart implemented these steps and observed significant improvement.
- 09:30–09:36 PT: token emit latency returned to baseline for most sessions.

Customer impact
- Estimated affected sessions: 12% of active streaming sessions in BrightCart's us-west-2 region during the window. Average stall: 6–12s. Duration: ~25 minutes of elevated risk.

Permanent fixes (timeline)
- Short-term (1–2 weeks): implement automated noisy-tenant detection + aggressive fairness enforcement for streaming RPCs (engineering owner: Marissa Cole).
- Medium-term (4–8 weeks): refine kernel-level I/O scheduling and provide configurable model isolation knobs to prevent co-tenancy I/O bleed for streaming endpoints (owner: Runtime Eng).

SLA credits and next steps
- Per our SLA, this event qualifies for a partial service credit. I'll open a credit request with Finance and copy you on the HubSpot ticket (HubSpot: contact/BRG-9421). Expect a formal credit offer in 3–5 business days.

Attachments & links
- Redwood interim postmortem: redwood-postmortem-20260815.pdf (attachment)
- Telemetry and raw logs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bBrightCartIncidentLogs
- Support ticket: HubSpot: contact/BRG-9421

Immediate owners and ETA
- Marissa Cole (SRE): noisy-tenant auto-detect and rule enforcement — ETA 2 weeks (2026-08-30).
- Runtime Engineering: kernel I/O scheduling changes — ETA 6 weeks (2026-09-27).

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the postmortem and the credit process.

Again, sorry for the disruption — we appreciate your patience and the swift verification on your side.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference
